A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IPR-1 and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v3 includes supplementary Sections 8–12, which were included in this comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.5 report original PhysCode validation, comparative gameplay results, zero-shot scaling, and component ablations.

after.justification: V3 reports original gameplay experiments and adds GRPO controls, value-prediction and representation ablations, transfer analyses, and qualitative case studies.

M1.justification: Supplementary Section 10.1 adds an auxiliary temporal head predicting feature changes, a training component absent from v1's method description. The central PhysCode, latent world model, Qwen3-VL-8B, GRPO, and rollout-based action-selection pipeline remains unchanged; most other supplementary specifications are implementation disclosures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same reported coverage: 863 retro, 134 HTML/Canvas, and three commercial games, evaluated through Survival, Curiosity, and Utility. The supplementary analyses partition or inspect this existing coverage rather than establish an additional dataset or task family.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Qwen3-VL-8B without IPR while retaining the existing comparator families. Table 3 adds VLM + GRPO and VLM + BC + GRPO controls. The Qwen3-VL-A30B label in v1 corresponds to the retained Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B comparator.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes reporting to random-zero/human-one normalization across objectives, replaces higher-is-better normalized ranks with lower-is-better average ranks, and adds an overall rank. Supplementary experiments introduce codebook sweeps, encoder configurations, and value-prediction evaluation. Section 10.5 inconsistently specifies 20 and 50 held-out games, so an actual split-size change cannot be established.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained PhysCode tests and scaling analysis, v3 adds GRPO controls, latent-versus-pixel value prediction, codebook-size sensitivity, encoder-pretraining comparisons, representation visualizations, and factor-wise transfer analysis. Section 12 and Figures 14–24 add extensive success and failure case studies, including IPR's difficulties with simultaneous threats.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional averaged results and qualitative claims of significant differences do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially changes scores and rankings: IPR's Survival/Curiosity/Utility means change from 0.589/7.874/0.178 to 0.252/1.173/0.493. These are revised results under changed reporting, not directly comparable performance gains. New GRPO rows, Tables 4–6, and supplementary analyses add further findings; Table 1 and the scaling curve remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The core POMDP formalization and main method equations are retained. Section 9.3 adds a specific power-of-ten definition of the survival reference horizon, and Section 11.2 defines code usage through a 0.1% assignment threshold. These are limited formal definitions; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The G2U, IPR, and PhysCode contributions and scaling/generalization claims remain. The headline performance claim strengthens from matching GPT-5 overall and surpassing it on Curiosity to surpassing GPT-5 overall.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations concerning latent representations filtering visual distractions, in-domain encoder training, codebook capacity, and structural versus mechanical transfer. It also identifies new failure boundaries involving rapid collisions, visual clutter, and multiple simultaneous threats, extending v1's limitations concerning games and short-horizon imagination.

D1.justification: Sections 9–10 supply recording and preprocessing procedures, baseline adaptations and prompts, architecture specifications, training budgets, sampling settings, and router calibration details largely absent from v1. Examples include 500k PhysCode training steps and eight action candidates. These disclosures do not themselves establish changed experiments. V3 also supplies project/demo access information.

R1.justification: The expanded introduction and supplementary discussion substantially broaden research positioning, including comparisons with Genie-2/3, SIMA/SIMA-2, Lumine, CombatVLA, and pi-star-0.6. They develop IPR's relationship to latent world models and generalist agents around shared physical and causal invariants, beyond v1's shorter discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, developing a longer argument across control, reinforcement learning, VLMs, and world models. Supplementary Sections 8–12 introduce a structured explanatory treatment of positioning, benchmark construction, implementation, analyses, and cases, although much of the main method text remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redesigned and its failure-case panel becomes Figure 3. Table 2 gains revised headers, group coloring, and an overall-rank column. V3 adds word clouds, benchmark and recording-tool illustrations, representation and transfer plots, three ablation tables, and extensive case-study sequences. Existing pipeline and scaling figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The added GRPO controls in Table 3 better separate prediction benefits from optimizer choice, while supplementary ablations, implementation details, and explicit failure cases strengthen evidence and transparency. The net improvement is limited by unreconciled metric descriptions across Table 2 and Sections 5.1/9.3, and the conflicting 20-versus-50-game specification in Section 10.5.
